extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step checklist for independent authors to take a near-final manuscript through editorial, production, and distribution stages for both print and ebook editions, with timing and file-format guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript readiness (starting point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the checklist at the point where you have a reasonably final manuscript that does not require higher level editing or significant revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist assumes a near-final draft; if significant developmental or structural edits remain, address those before moving into copyediting, design, and production. This is the point at which to begin formal production planning and booking service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting (formal copyedit recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek a formal copyedit from a professional freelance copyeditor who will focus on style, grammar, consistency, and possibly light fact-checking (especially for nonfiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical copyedit for an 80,000-word manuscript takes about two weeks; good copyeditors usually need to be booked a month (or more) in advance. Authors should allow at least one, preferably two, weeks to review and make changes after the copyedit is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front cover design and creative brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover is often the number-one marketing tool; research bestselling books similar to your own and prepare a creative brief for a designer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find at least two or three covers you like and write 50–100 words explaining why they work — this becomes the start of your brief. Finalize title, subtitle, and book description before or during cover work. Consider hiring a professional designer (though some authors use Canva).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book description variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize multiple lengths of the book description for use at retailers and on the back cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a very short description (25–50 words), a short one (50–100 words), and a longer one (~250 words) so you have appropriate blurbs for different retailer fields and marketing contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back cover and spine design (print editions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paperback/print-on-demand editions require a back cover and spine; hardcover may require additional design for flaps and wider spine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spine design cannot be finalized until page count is firm; page count and cover measurements depend on the printer, cover type, and interior paper. If using multiple vendors (e.g., Amazon KDP and IngramSpark), you may need different cover layout files for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance praise / blurbs timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to include advance praise or blurbs on the cover, gather them before the cover design process begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If blurbs are not ready, instruct the designer to use dummy text and plan to swap in actual blurbs later. Starting blurb-gathering early avoids last-minute design changes and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print interior design: template vs. custom
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to use a template or hire a custom interior designer based on the book's content and complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that are primarily body text (novels, memoirs) often do fine with basic/template designs (e.g., Joel Friedlander's templates) and using templates can cut production time (often by about one month). Nonfiction with many elements (illustrations, graphics, color) usually requires a custom interior designer to ensure correct file setup and reproduction values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-format consistency (print vs ebook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan how you'll ensure the same final text across print and ebook editions, especially if producing print in InDesign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: InDesign can export EPUB files but the process isn’t necessarily simple; hire a professional interior designer who knows how to export EPUBs from InDesign or hire an independent ebook formatter to avoid inconsistencies between editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design elements inventory and sample chapter approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a list of all design elements that occur in the book (e.g., chapter title/chapter opener, A head, B head, bulleted list, numbered list, block quote).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the designer show a sample or lay out a single chapter before proceeding with the full book so you can request revisions. Once the full book is laid out and you're confident text won't shift, then send files to an indexer if you want an index prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ebook design and file preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare ebook files (reflowable EPUBs) or hire a professional for fixed-layout or heavily illustrated titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many authors use Word plus retailer auto-conversion, or tools like Vellum, Calibre, or Sigil. If the title needs fixed layout or complex visuals, hire a pro. Budget at least one week to prepare ebook files if doing it yourself. Some cover/interior designers will also prepare ebook files for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofing strategy and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how thorough the proofing process will be and whether to hire a professional proofreader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If files are very clean and you have confidence no production errors were introduced, you might skip hiring a proofer. If you skipped the copyedit or you are the only person who has seen the files aside from the designer, hire a professional proofreader. Consider earlier proofing that starts before ebook design and file prep. Critically, determine whether you'll have access to final files — if a freelancer delivers final files you can't open or modify, you must provide very clean source files to avoid extra costs/delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata preparation (categories, pricing, descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do research and prep metadata in advance so you have all descriptive and sales information handy when publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide how you will describe the book, how it will be categorized, and your pricing strategy before entering retailer/distributor interfaces; have descriptions, category choices, BISAC, pricing, author bio, keywords, and other fields ready to avoid rushed decisions during upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required files for print-on-demand upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the full cover layout file (PDF) and full interior layout file (PDF) ready for your print-on-demand edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using both Amazon KDP and IngramSpark, prepare a different cover layout file for each because their measurements differ. Ensure PDFs meet the specific vendor's specs for bleed, spine dimensions, and color profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required files for ebook upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a front cover image (JPG, PNG, or other image format) and an ebook file; EPUB will give the best quality but many retailers accept Word documents and other formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPUB where possible for best results; check each retailer/distributor for accepted file types and recommended image dimensions/resolutions for covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading, release timing, and preorder options
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploading files and making the book available for sale is usually quick; know retailer-specific timing and preorder windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amazon often makes a book available within 24 hours; if not ready to go live, set a preorder and choose pub date. Amazon allows preorders up to 90 days in advance; other services (e.g., Smashwords) may allow up to one year. Be prepared with all metadata and files before starting the upload to avoid interruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and booking lead times
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan backward from your intended publication date and schedule time to book copyeditors, designers, proofers, and other vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many professionals (copyeditors, designers) need to be booked a month or more ahead. Use a deadline-driven checklist or interactive worksheet to auto-generate suggested deadlines for each step to help hit your target pub date.
